faq_entries.question: How are breaking API changes managed?
faq_entries.answer: Breaking changes are introduced only in new major API versions (for example /v1/ to /v2/). Each major version is supported for at least 18 months after its successor ships. Deprecation notices are sent via `Sunset` and `Deprecation` response headers and by email to API token owners 6 months before end-of-life.

faq_entries.question: How do I authenticate API requests?
faq_entries.answer: All API requests require a token in the Authorization header: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Tokens are generated under Account Settings > API Tokens and can be scoped to read, write, or admin permissions. Tokens expire after 90 days of inactivity.

faq_entries.question: How do I check my current rate limit status?
faq_entries.answer: Inspect these response headers on every call: `X-RateLimit-Limit` (plan requests-per-minute cap), `X-RateLimit-Remaining` (requests remaining in the window), and `X-RateLimit-Reset` (Unix timestamp when the window resets).

faq_entries.question: How do I export large datasets without timing out?
faq_entries.answer: Synchronous exports time out after 5 minutes. Use the Async Export API, which returns a job ID that can be polled for completion. For datasets exceeding 5 million rows, contact support to schedule a manual export.

faq_entries.question: How do I paginate through large result sets?
faq_entries.answer: List endpoints use cursor-based pagination. Use `?limit=N` (maximum 100) for page size. The response includes `next_cursor` and `has_more`; pass `next_cursor` as `?cursor=<value>` in the next request.

faq_entries.question: What are the API rate limits?
faq_entries.answer: Default per-token limits: Free 60 requests/minute (burst 10); Professional 600 requests/minute (burst 100); Enterprise 6,000 requests/minute (burst 1,000). Limits use a token-bucket algorithm with soft limits (short bursts above the stated rate) and a hard ceiling at 2x the stated rate. Enterprise plans can request custom limits above 6,000 RPM.

faq_entries.question: What happens when I exceed the API rate limit?
faq_entries.answer: The API returns HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) with a `Retry-After` header indicating how many seconds to wait. Repeated violations may temporarily suspend the API token. For CI/CD pipelines, stagger test suites (for example, 1-second delays between calls) or upgrade to an Enterprise plan for higher limits.

faq_entries.question: What HTTP methods are supported?
faq_entries.answer: GET (retrieve), POST (create), PUT (full update), PATCH (partial update), DELETE (remove). All endpoints return JSON; POST/PUT/PATCH bodies must use `Content-Type: application/json`.

faq_entries.question: What is the maximum payload size for API requests?
faq_entries.answer: The maximum REST API request payload is 10 MB. File uploads through the Assets API are limited to 250 MB per file. Requests above these limits return HTTP 413 (Payload Too Large).

faq_entries.question: Why does my API token return 403 Forbidden for POST requests?
faq_entries.answer: A token that works for GET but returns 403 for POST is usually read-only. Go to Account Settings > API Tokens, edit the token, and enable the `write` scope. Tokens created before v4.0 defaulted to read-only.

faq_entries.question: Can I sign up using my Google or GitHub account?
faq_entries.answer: Yes. On the signup page choose "Continue with Google" or "Continue with GitHub" and authenticate with the provider. On first login, complete the organization profile. SSO-managed organizations may restrict social login options.

faq_entries.question: Can I use Single Sign-On (SSO) with my corporate identity provider?
faq_entries.answer: Yes. The platform supports SAML 2.0 and OIDC-based SSO. An organization's IT administrator configures the identity provider integration; once configured, users in that domain see a "Sign in with SSO" button on the login page.

faq_entries.question: How do I create a new account?
faq_entries.answer: Visit https://app.platform.example.com/signup, enter a work email address, choose a password (minimum 12 characters with uppercase, lowercase, digit, and special character), and accept the Terms of Service. A verification email is sent; click the link within 24 hours to activate the account. After activation, set up the organization profile and invite team members.

faq_entries.question: How do I enable Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)?
faq_entries.answer: Go to Account Settings > Security > Two-Factor Authentication and click "Enable 2FA". Choose an authenticator app (recommended) or SMS verification. Scan the QR code or enter the phone number, then enter the verification code to confirm. Download and store the recovery codes securely; they are required if the device is lost.

faq_entries.question: How do I manage multiple organization memberships?
faq_entries.answer: If you belong to multiple organizations, an organization switcher appears in the top-left corner of the dashboard after login. Each organization keeps separate settings, projects, and billing. A single account can belong to up to 10 organizations.

faq_entries.question: How do I reset my platform password?
faq_entries.answer: Navigate to the login page and click "Forgot Password". Enter your registered email address; a reset link valid for 30 minutes is sent. Click the link, enter a new password (minimum 12 characters with uppercase, lowercase, digit, and special character), and confirm; the password updates immediately. If the email does not arrive, check the spam folder first, verify the email address on the account, and note that the link expires after 30 minutes. If the issue persists, an administrator can trigger a manual reset from the user management panel.

faq_entries.question: I cannot log in after my company enforced SSO. What should I do?
faq_entries.answer: When an organization enforces SSO, existing password-based accounts are linked to the SSO identity by email address. Sign in with the "Sign in with SSO" button using corporate credentials. If an error occurs, the IT administrator may need to add the account to the SSO provisioning group; otherwise contact the internal helpdesk.

faq_entries.question: I lost my phone or authenticator app and cannot log in. How do I recover my account?
faq_entries.answer: Use a recovery code to regain access; recovery codes are issued during 2FA setup. If the recovery codes are also lost, an account administrator can disable 2FA from the admin panel. For accounts without an administrator, identity verification using a government ID is required to reset 2FA.

faq_entries.question: What redirect URI should I configure for SSO?
faq_entries.answer: As of v4.2.0 the SSO redirect URI format is `https://app.platform.example.com/auth/sso/callback?provider=<idp_id>`. The previous format (`/auth/callback/sso`) is outdated.

faq_entries.question: Why am I getting "Invalid Credentials" after resetting my password?
faq_entries.answer: "Invalid Credentials" after a reset is usually caused by cached old credentials. Clear the browser cache and cookies and try again. Verify Caps Lock is off and that the correct email address is being used. The system locks accounts for 15 minutes after 5 failed attempts.

faq_entries.question: Why is my SSO login stuck in an infinite redirect loop?
faq_entries.answer: An infinite redirect between the IdP and the login page usually indicates a SAML assertion mismatch. Verify that the NameID format in the IdP matches the platform expectation (emailAddress), and confirm that the Assertion Consumer Service (ACS) URL in the IdP configuration matches the platform metadata exactly.

faq_entries.question: Can I switch from monthly to annual billing?
faq_entries.answer: In Account Settings > Billing > Plan Details, select "Switch to Annual Billing". The annual rate is charged immediately, and remaining days on the monthly plan are credited toward the annual amount. Annual billing provides a 15% discount versus monthly billing.

faq_entries.question: How do I add or change the billing contact?
faq_entries.answer: Go to Account Settings > Billing > Billing Contacts and click "Add Contact" to add a billing contact by email. To change the primary contact, select the contact and click "Set as Primary". The primary contact receives all invoices, payment receipts, and billing notifications.

faq_entries.question: How do I upgrade my subscription plan?
faq_entries.answer: Go to Account Settings > Billing > Plan Details, click "Change Plan", and select the desired tier. The price difference is prorated for the remainder of the billing cycle, and new features take effect immediately. Downgrades apply at the start of the next billing cycle.

faq_entries.question: How does the free trial work?
faq_entries.answer: The 14-day free trial includes full access to all Professional plan features and does not require a credit card. Reminder emails are sent on day 7 and day 13. At the end of the trial the account is downgraded to the Free tier unless a payment method is added and a paid plan selected.

faq_entries.question: Is there a spending limit I can set?
faq_entries.answer: Yes. For usage-based charges (extra API requests, additional storage) set a monthly spending cap in Account Settings > Billing > Spending Limits. When the cap is reached, usage-based features are throttled rather than billed further. Warnings are sent at 50%, 80%, and 100% of the cap.

faq_entries.question: What happens if my payment fails?
faq_entries.answer: A failed payment triggers an immediate email notification. The system retries after 3 days. If the second attempt fails, the account enters a 7-day grace period with all features available; afterwards write access is restricted until the payment is resolved. Update the payment method in Account Settings > Billing > Payment Methods.

faq_entries.question: What is the SLA uptime guarantee?
faq_entries.answer: Free tier: best effort, no SLA. Professional: 99.5% uptime. Enterprise: 99.95% uptime with financial credits for breach. SLAs are measured on a calendar-month basis, excluding scheduled maintenance windows.

faq_entries.question: What payment methods are accepted?
faq_entries.answer: Visa, Mastercard, American Express, and bank transfer (ACH/wire) for annual plans are accepted. Enterprise customers can also use purchase orders with Net-30 terms after credit approval. Payment methods are managed under Account Settings > Billing > Payment Methods.

faq_entries.question: Where can I find my invoices?
faq_entries.answer: Invoices are available under Account Settings > Billing > Invoice History, where PDF copies can be downloaded for any billing period. Invoices are also emailed to the billing contact on file within 24 hours of payment processing.

faq_entries.question: Why is my invoice amount higher than my plan price?
faq_entries.answer: The plan price is the base charge; additional charges can come from extra API requests beyond plan limits, additional storage beyond allocation, or add-on services. Review the line items under Account Settings > Billing > Invoice History for the detailed breakdown.

faq_entries.question: How do I add custom health checks to my deployment?
faq_entries.answer: Define health check endpoints in `deploy.yaml` under the `health_checks` section. HTTP, TCP, and command-based checks are supported with configurable intervals, timeouts, and retry counts.

faq_entries.question: How do I configure database connection pooling?
faq_entries.answer: Set `DB_POOL_SIZE` (maximum connections, default 20), `DB_POOL_TIMEOUT` (seconds to wait for a connection, default 30), and `DB_POOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT` (seconds before idle connections close, default 300).

faq_entries.question: How do I configure environment variables for a deployment?
faq_entries.answer: Environment variables can be set at project, environment, or service scope. Service-level overrides environment-level, which overrides project-level. Use the `--scope` flag to specify the level.

faq_entries.question: How do I deploy on Kubernetes?
faq_entries.answer: An official Helm chart is published at `helm.platform.example.com`. Add the repository with `helm repo add platform https://charts.platform.example.com`, then install with `helm install my-deployment platform/platform-stack`.

faq_entries.question: How do I deploy to production?
faq_entries.answer: Production deployments follow change management: 1) Create a release candidate from staging (`git checkout staging && git pull && git checkout -b release/vX.Y.Z`). 2) Open a production change request. 3) Obtain approval from Tech Lead, QA Lead, and Operations Lead. 4) During the Tue/Thu 10:00-12:00 UTC window, merge to main, monitor the canary (10% traffic for 15 minutes), proceed to full rollout if metrics are green, and monitor dashboards for 30 minutes.

faq_entries.question: How do I deploy to staging?
faq_entries.answer: 1) Ensure all tests pass on the feature branch. 2) Open a merge request targeting `staging`. 3) Wait for the CI/CD pipeline, including integration tests. 4) After merge the staging environment auto-deploys. 5) Verify with `curl https://staging.internal.example.com/healthz`. 6) Run `./scripts/smoke-test-staging.sh`.

faq_entries.question: How do I deploy using Docker Compose?
faq_entries.answer: 1) Download `docker-compose.yml` from the releases page. 2) Create a `.env` file with the required environment variables. 3) Run `docker compose up -d`. 4) Access the application at `http://localhost:8080`. 5) Run `curl http://localhost:8080/healthz`.

faq_entries.question: How do I roll back a deployment?
faq_entries.answer: 1) Identify the last known-good commit in the deployment history. 2) Run `./scripts/rollback-production.sh <commit-hash>`; the script restores the matching artifact, runs database migration reversions where applicable, and executes health checks. Alternatively, use `platform-cli rollback --deployment <id> --env production` and verify with `platform-cli health-check --env production`. 3) Notify `#platform-incidents` and create a post-mortem within 24 hours.

faq_entries.question: How do I start a new deployment?
faq_entries.answer: 1) Define the deployment configuration in `deploy.yaml`. 2) Validate it with `platform-cli validate --config deploy.yaml`. 3) Execute with `platform-cli deploy --config deploy.yaml --env staging`. 4) Monitor progress with `platform-cli status --deployment <id>`.

faq_entries.question: What are the minimum hardware requirements for self-hosted deployment?
faq_entries.answer: Minimum: 4 vCPUs (x86_64 or ARM64), 8 GB RAM (16 GB recommended for production), 50 GB SSD for the application plus attachment storage, and a 1 Gbps low-latency connection to the database.

faq_entries.question: What breaking changes were introduced in v4.0.0?
faq_entries.answer: v4.0.0 (2025-01-06) deprecated API v1 endpoints (sunset 2026-07-06), replaced the legacy webhook format with JSON Schema v2 payloads, raised the minimum TLS version to 1.2, and ended Python 3.7/3.8 SDK support.

faq_entries.question: What database engines are supported?
faq_entries.answer: PostgreSQL 14.x, 15.x, and 16.x (recommended); MySQL 8.0.x (InnoDB required); SQL Server 2019 and 2022 (Enterprise tier only).

faq_entries.question: What is the difference between blue-green and canary deployments?
faq_entries.answer: Blue-green runs two complete environments and switches traffic at once. Canary gradually shifts a percentage of traffic to the new version. The platform defaults to canary for production and blue-green for staging.

faq_entries.question: What operating systems are supported?
faq_entries.answer: Ubuntu 20.04/22.04/24.04 LTS; RHEL 8.x/9.x and compatible derivatives (Rocky Linux, AlmaLinux); Debian 11 (Bullseye) and 12 (Bookworm); container deployment via Docker 24+ or Kubernetes 1.27+.

faq_entries.question: What was added in v4.1.0?
faq_entries.answer: v4.1.0 (2025-02-01) added WebSocket real-time notifications for deployment events, multi-region failover for Enterprise, SAML metadata auto-refresh for IdP certificate rotation, and a customizable dashboard layout.

faq_entries.question: What's new in v4.2.0?
faq_entries.answer: v4.2.0 (2025-03-01) added bulk user import via CSV (maximum 10,000 users per import), custom RBAC role definitions, fuzzy search with typo tolerance, and audit log export to S3-compatible storage.

faq_entries.question: How do I access the Kibana logs dashboard?
faq_entries.answer: Navigate to https://kibana.internal.example.com and sign in with SSO credentials. The "Platform Logs" dashboard shows all application logs; use the filter bar to narrow by service, environment, or trace ID.

faq_entries.question: How do I configure webhook notifications?
faq_entries.answer: Configure webhooks under Developer Settings > Webhooks. Click "Add Webhook", provide the target URL, select events (minimum: `deployment.completed`, `build.failed`), and optionally set a secret token for signature verification. The platform sends a test ping; the endpoint must answer an initial challenge-response handshake within 5 seconds or the webhook is not created. Payloads are signed with HMAC-SHA256 using the provided secret.

faq_entries.question: What integrations are available out of the box?
faq_entries.answer: Native integrations include GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Slack, Jira, PagerDuty, Datadog, and Splunk. The Integration Marketplace offers 200+ community and partner integrations. Custom integrations can be built with the Webhook API and Platform SDK.

faq_entries.question: Why is my webhook not firing for deployment events?
faq_entries.answer: Confirm the webhook is enabled and the event filter includes `deployment.completed`. By default the webhook fires only for successful deployments; enable "Include Failed Deployments" to receive failed ones. Also confirm the endpoint passed the initial challenge-response handshake when the webhook was created.

faq_entries.question: Why was RabbitMQ chosen over Kafka for the task queue?
faq_entries.answer: RabbitMQ was chosen for mature AMQP 0-9-1 support, flexible routing with exchanges and bindings, and lower operational complexity for task distribution with individual acknowledgment. Kafka was considered overengineered for throughput below 10K messages/second and added operational burden.

faq_entries.question: How do I troubleshoot connection timeouts to the API?
faq_entries.answer: Verify connectivity with `ping api.platform.example.com`. If ping succeeds but API calls time out, check whether a firewall or proxy blocks outbound HTTPS on port 443, and confirm DNS resolution with `nslookup api.platform.example.com`. For persistent issues, collect a HAR file from the browser developer tools and attach it to a support ticket.

faq_entries.question: What IP ranges should I whitelist for platform access?
faq_entries.answer: Whitelist these CIDR ranges: 203.0.113.0/24 (primary API and web), 203.0.114.0/24 (WebSocket connections), and 198.51.100.0/24 (file storage and CDN). Ranges may change with 30 days' notice via the status page.

faq_entries.question: Why do WebSocket connections keep dropping?
faq_entries.answer: WebSocket disconnections are commonly caused by load balancer timeouts, proxy limits, or NAT gateway idle timeouts. Allow persistent connections for at least 60 seconds of idle time. The platform sends WebSocket ping frames every 30 seconds to keep the connection alive.

faq_entries.question: How do I add a new team member to the GitLab group?
faq_entries.answer: Go to Group Settings > Members > Invite Members. Enter the email, select a role (Developer for engineers, Reporter for PMs), and set an expiration (default 365 days). The person receives an invitation email.

faq_entries.question: How do I request access to production systems?
faq_entries.answer: Submit an access request through the IT Service Portal at https://it.internal.example.com/access. Select "Production Infrastructure Access" and provide team, systems, access level (read-only, operator, admin), and business justification. Manager approval is required, and access is reviewed quarterly.

faq_entries.question: How do I set up my local development environment?
faq_entries.answer: 1) `git clone git@gitlab.internal.example.com:platform/docs.git`. 2) Install Python 3.11+, Docker 24+, and Node.js 20 LTS. 3) Run `./scripts/setup-dev-env.sh`. 4) Configure `.env.local` with development API keys. 5) Start services with `docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d`. 6) Verify with `./scripts/health-check.sh`.

faq_entries.question: How do new users get started with the platform?
faq_entries.answer: After account creation, complete the Quick Start wizard from the dashboard welcome banner. It guides you through connecting a source repository, configuring the first deployment pipeline, and inviting team members; estimated completion time is 15 minutes.

faq_entries.question: What is the branch naming convention?
faq_entries.answer: Feature: `feature/YYYY-MM-DD-brief-description`. Bug fix: `fix/ISSUE-NUMBER-brief-description`. Hotfix: `hotfix/YYYY-MM-DD-brief-description`. Release: `release/vX.Y.Z`. Branch from `main`, rebase before merge, and squash commits for all merge requests.

faq_entries.question: Does the platform support wildcard certificates?
faq_entries.answer: Yes. Wildcard certificates (`*.example.com`) are supported for custom domains and are uploaded the same way as standard certificates. A wildcard covers one level of subdomain (for example `app.example.com` but not `api.app.example.com`).

faq_entries.question: How do I enable audit logging?
faq_entries.answer: Audit logging is available on Enterprise plans under Settings > Security > Audit Logs. Enable "Detailed Activity Logging" and select event categories: Authentication Events, API Access, Configuration Changes, and Data Export. Logs are retained 90 days by default, configurable up to 365 days on request.

faq_entries.question: How do I upload a custom SSL certificate for my custom domain?
faq_entries.answer: Go to Settings > Domains > SSL Certificates and click "Upload Certificate". Provide the PEM certificate, private key, and intermediate chain files. The system validates validity, chain of trust, and private-key match before activating. Renewal reminders are sent 30, 14, and 7 days before expiry.

faq_entries.question: How does the platform distribute data across database servers?
faq_entries.answer: Data is distributed across multiple database servers to provide horizontal scalability and strong consistency for single-tenant queries. Detailed sharding internals are not published; they are available to enterprise customers under NDA.

faq_entries.question: How does the platform handle data residency requirements?
faq_entries.answer: Enterprise customers select a data residency region during onboarding. Available regions: US (us-east-1, us-west-2), EU (eu-central-1, eu-west-1), and APAC (ap-southeast-1, ap-northeast-1). Data at rest is encrypted with AES-256 and in transit with TLS 1.2+. Customer data stays in the selected region except for explicit cross-region replication configured by the customer.

faq_entries.question: What are the database backup schedules?
faq_entries.answer: Full backups run daily at 02:00 UTC and incremental backups every 4 hours. Retention is 30 days for daily backups, 7 days for incremental backups, and 12 months for monthly backups.

faq_entries.question: What TLS and cipher configuration does the platform support?
faq_entries.answer: The platform supports modern, secure TLS configurations only. TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1, SSLv3, RC4, and 3DES are disabled on all endpoints. The detailed cipher-suite list is available in the enterprise security whitepaper under NDA.

faq_entries.question: Why does my custom SSL certificate fail browser validation?
faq_entries.answer: Common causes: (1) the intermediate certificate chain is missing, so the bundle must include all intermediate CA certificates; (2) the certificate is issued for a different domain; (3) the private key does not match the certificate. An SSL checker tool can identify the specific failure.

faq_entries.question: How do I clear the Redis cache safely?
faq_entries.answer: 1) Check memory: `redis-cli -h <host> INFO memory | grep used_memory_human`. 2) With `allkeys-lru`, Redis evicts automatically; otherwise clear the current database with `redis-cli -h <host> FLUSHDB`. `FLUSHALL` clears every database and must never be used in production without explicit approval. 3) Monitor for increased database load while caches rebuild.

faq_entries.question: How do I declare a SEV1 incident?
faq_entries.answer: Declare a SEV1 with `/incident declare` in Slack or by calling the emergency hotline at extension 4911. Provide the affected service, observed symptoms, approximate start time, and any known recent changes.

faq_entries.question: How do I diagnose high database CPU usage?
faq_entries.answer: 1) Count active connections: `SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state = 'active';`. 2) Find long-running queries: `SELECT pid, now() - query_start AS duration, query FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state = 'active' ORDER BY duration DESC LIMIT 10;`. 3) Check locks: `SELECT * FROM pg_locks WHERE NOT granted;`. 4) Terminate a problematic query with `SELECT pg_terminate_backend(<pid>);`. Common causes are missing indexes, unoptimized joins over large tables, and analytics queries during peak hours.

faq_entries.question: How do I set up alerting?
faq_entries.answer: Suggested thresholds: API error rate >1% for 5 minutes pages on-call; p99 latency >1s for 10 minutes creates an incident ticket; disk usage >85% sends a warning; database replication lag >30s pages on-call; certificate expiry within 7 days emails the security team.

faq_entries.question: How often are SLOs reviewed?
faq_entries.answer: SLOs are reviewed quarterly by the platform reliability team. Adjustments require approval from the VP of Engineering.

faq_entries.question: What happens when an SLO is violated?
faq_entries.answer: An incident is created automatically in the on-call rotation. The error-budget burn rate is calculated and alerts go to the platform-eng Slack channel.

faq_entries.question: What is the incident communication template?
faq_entries.answer: Post to `#platform-incidents`: `SEV<level>: <brief description>. Impact: <user-facing impact>. Investigating: <team/engineer>. Next update: <time>` (typically 30 minutes for SEV1 and 1 hour for SEV2). Updates go in the thread.

faq_entries.question: What logging levels should I use?
faq_entries.answer: ERROR for errors needing immediate attention; WARN for degraded functionality or approaching limits; INFO for normal operational events such as deployments and signups; DEBUG for detailed diagnostics (disabled in production). Logs must be structured JSON with at least timestamp, level, service, trace_id, and message.

faq_entries.question: What metrics should I monitor for the platform?
faq_entries.answer: Track application request rate, error rate, latency (p50/p95/p99), and active connections; infrastructure CPU, memory, disk I/O, and network throughput; database connection-pool utilization, query latency, replication lag, and deadlocks; and business metrics such as active users, feature adoption, and API token usage.

faq_entries.question: What should I do when the API returns 502 Bad Gateway?
faq_entries.answer: A 502 means the API gateway cannot reach the backend. 1) Check pods: `kubectl get pods -n platform -l app=api-backend`. 2) Check readiness: `kubectl describe pod <pod-name> -n platform`. 3) Read logs: `kubectl logs -n platform -l app=api-backend --tail=200`. 4) If crash-looping, inspect `State:` in the pod description. Common causes are database connection pool exhaustion, memory limits, and configuration errors after a deploy.

faq_entries.question: Why does my Docker container exit immediately with code 137?
faq_entries.answer: Exit code 137 indicates the container was killed by the OOM (Out of Memory) killer. Check that at least 2 GB of memory is allocated to the container. Increase the memory limit in the Docker configuration, or add a swap file if memory is constrained.

faq_entries.question: Why is the dashboard slow to load?
faq_entries.answer: The dashboard aggregates data across all projects. For users with 50+ projects, enable "Lazy Load" under User Preferences > Dashboard to load project data on demand as sections are expanded.
